name: Alabama
regulatoryNotes: Alabama requires a 10-day free look period for life insurance policies. The state mandates that insurers notify policyholders 30 days before cancellation.

name: Alaska
regulatoryNotes: Alaska provides a 10-day free look period. The state has unique provisions for remote area residents and allows electronic policy delivery.

name: Arizona
regulatoryNotes: Arizona requires a 10-day free look period. The state has strict anti-discrimination laws preventing denial based on genetic information.

name: Arkansas
regulatoryNotes: Arkansas requires a 10-day free look period for life insurance. Policies must include a grace period of at least 31 days for premium payments.

name: California
regulatoryNotes: California provides a 30-day free look period — one of the longest in the US. The state's Department of Insurance actively regulates premium increases and requires extensive disclosures.

name: Colorado
regulatoryNotes: Colorado requires a 10-day free look period. The state mandates mental health parity in insurance policies and has strong consumer protection laws.

name: Connecticut
regulatoryNotes: Connecticut provides a 10-day free look period. Hartford, CT is known as the insurance capital of the US, and the state has extensive insurance regulations.

name: Delaware
regulatoryNotes: Delaware provides a 10-day free look period. The state is home to many insurance holding companies due to favorable business laws.

name: Florida
regulatoryNotes: Florida provides a 14-day free look period. The state has unique hurricane-related provisions and strong protections for seniors regarding life insurance.

name: Georgia
regulatoryNotes: Georgia requires a 10-day free look period. The state has strong insurance fraud statutes and requires carriers to respond to claims within 15 days.

name: Hawaii
regulatoryNotes: Hawaii provides a 10-day free look period. The state has a unique employer-mandate for health insurance and special provisions for the island-based insurance market.

name: Idaho
regulatoryNotes: Idaho provides a 10-day free look period. The state has relatively straightforward insurance regulations with low premium taxes.

name: Illinois
regulatoryNotes: Illinois requires a 10-day free look period. The state has a robust insurance regulatory framework and provides protections for senior citizens including a 30-day free look for policies sold to those over 60.

name: Indiana
regulatoryNotes: Indiana requires a 10-day free look period. The state has competitive insurance markets and relatively lower average premiums due to lower cost of living.

name: Iowa

name: Kansas

name: Kentucky

name: Louisiana

name: Maine
regulatoryNotes: Maine provides a 10-day free look period. The state has consumer-friendly insurance regulations and strong protections for policyholders.

name: Maryland

name: Massachusetts

name: Michigan

name: Minnesota

name: Mississippi

name: Missouri

name: Montana

name: Nevada

name: New Hampshire

name: New Jersey

name: New Mexico

name: New York

name: Pennsylvania

name: Rhode Island
